newsitem.title: USA: American Air pleased by union leaders' vote.
newsitem.headline: American Air pleased by union leaders' vote.

text.p: American Airlines welcomed the acceptance by pilots' union leaders of a tentative labor agreement, raising hopes that a bitter labor dispute is close to an end.

"The tentative agreement reflects compromise and creativity from both sides," airline president Donald J. Carty said in a statement shortly after leaders of the Allied Pilots Association (APA) approved a tentative agreement hammered out by both sides last month.

The contract deal will be sent to rank-and-file pilots within six weeks for their approval. Their rejection of the deal would bring a summer strike at the carrier but union officials said they are confident the new deal will be accepted.
Carty said both sides had "worked very hard to find a way to meet our competitive needs and answer APA's concerns, and this agreement does both."

The contract includes a nine percent wage increase over five years and a stock option program for pilots, while American, a unit of AMR Corp, will be able to buy regional jets for its lower-cost commuter carrier.
